(1) TOTAL -1: exactly one PRE-EXISTING rule left the profile, `streaming_concatenation` — IEEE 1364-2005 has no streaming concatenation at all ('streaming' occurs 0 times in its Annex A). The 13 NEW `_sv_only` rules are `[sv_2017, sv_2023]` and so are not in this profile's population; sv_2017 satisfiability rose 1388 -> 1401 and sv_2023 1410 -> 1423, both by exactly the rules added, with NO other pre-existing rule's satisfiable set moving. cases.note: SV-0021 regression lock: an implicit-type ANSI port (`input a`) followed by an explicitly-typed ANSI port (`output reg b`) — `module m (input a, output reg b);`. Valid IEEE 1364-2005 (ANSI port declarations with a `reg` type, A.1.3) and valid IEEE 1800, so it accepts under EVERY profile. SV-0021 was an all-profile over-REJECTION (the whole ANSI header rejected, historical furthest_position=25) fixed as a CONSEQUENCE of SV-0037 (SV-KEYWORD-PRIMARY-FIDELITY.3.1, 1.0.162->1.0.163): the greedy ungated `net_type_identifier` in `net_port_type_sv_2017/2023` ate the implicit port's name under the global longest_match policy, corrupting the first port into a `nonansi` shape so the following explicitly-typed ANSI port had no valid continuation. Routing alt-1 to the store-gated `checked_nettype_identifier` let the implicit `ansi` path win; this lock pins that the mixed implicit-then-typed ANSI header stays accepting. Adjudicated at SV-OVER-REJECTION-FIDELITY.1.

SV-0033 no-over-gate control: ranged packed (`reg [7:0] q;`) and ranged unpacked (`reg r [3:0];`) dimensions are legal IEEE 1364-2005 (§4.9/A.2.5) and MUST still accept under verilog_2005 — the .6.9 gate targets only `unsized_dimension` (`[]`), never `packed_dimension`/`unpacked_dimension`'s ranged forms. Also the no-over-gate control for SV-0034 (.6.10): gating `associative_dimension`/`queue_dimension` must not affect the ranged unpacked form.

`-> e;` is the legal IEEE 1364-2005 event trigger. Blocking `->` form; parses under every profile (relabeled kind:"non_blocking"->"blocking" at SV-OVER-REJECTION-FIDELITY.3 per IEEE 1800 §15.5.3, parse-verdict unchanged).

SV-0023 lock: `-> e[0];` event-array trigger. ACCEPTS under verilog_2005 (IEEE 1364-2005 A.6.5 `-> hei { [ expression ] } ;`, bracket array-selects — closed at SV-OVER-REJECTION-FIDELITY.3 by giving event_trigger_verilog_2005 a trailing bit_select) and under sv_2023 (Annex A adds a trailing nonrange_select). REJECTS under sv_2017 (IEEE 1800-2017 A.6.5 is `-> hei ;` with NO select — faithful strict-2017 subset; the 2023 LRM added the select).

SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.4 control: the half of the construct the signing gate must NOT touch. IEEE 1364-2005 A.2.1.3 derives `integer i;` (:152) and `time t;` (:174), and A.2.2.1 `variable_type` (:185-187) derives the `= constant_expression` initialiser. A fix that gated `integer_atom_type` itself instead of the optional `signing` beside it turns this REJECT.

The ~48 SV-only reserved words (`bit`, `int`, `class`, ...) are legal IEEE 1364-2005 identifiers (the D2 un-reserve axis); the sv_2017/sv_2023 `reject` rows are spec-correct because those words ARE reserved there. `initial assert (1);` is a legal 1364-2005 task enable of a task named `assert`.
The minimal module; also the alias-normalization accept probe.

SV-0024 lock (positive): `module m ({a, b});` — the braced concatenation port (`{ port_reference {, port_reference} }`) is the LRM's valid multi-reference form and accepts under EVERY profile. Before SV-LRM-SHAPE-FIDELITY.1 the missing `lbrace`/`rbrace` made this REJECT while the invalid un-braced `a b` accepted; the fix inverts both.

SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.4 control: the sibling `data_type` alternative where signing IS legal in IEEE 1364-2005 — A.2.1.3 `reg_declaration ::= reg [ signed ] [ range ] list_of_variable_identifiers ;` (:172). Pins the gate to the ATOM branch (`integer_atom_type ( signing )?`) rather than the VECTOR branch (`integer_vector_type ( signing )? packed_dimension*`) beside it.

All 12 IEEE specify timing checks in their LRM `$` spellings (1364-2005 §15 / 1800-2017 §31) — the SV-0029 wave-1 accept-lock (SV-DOLLAR-LRM-FIDELITY.2): before that fix the mangled `sv_dollar_*` token literals wrongly REJECTED every LRM spelling.

The IEEE scalar timing-check compare forms (== / === / != / !== against scalar_constant, 1364-2005 / 1800-2017 A.7.5.3) plus the `e == 1'b0 && f` flat-fallback form — the SV-0030 accept-lock (SV-DOLLAR-LRM-FIDELITY.3): acceptance was never lost, but the compare forms now emit the typed eq/case_eq/ne/case_ne shapes instead of a flat expression, and the !binary_operator follow-guard keeps operator-continued conditions on the flat branch.

The IEEE UDP init_val digit alternatives 1'b0 / 1'b1 (1364-2005 / 1800-2017 A.5.1) — the SV-0030 second-site accept-lock (SV-DOLLAR-LRM-FIDELITY.3): before that fix the digit-less "1'b" token prefix-stole the spelling and `initial q = 1'b0;` REJECTED under every profile.
Legal 1364-2005 task enable of a user task named `wait_order` (un-reserved under the profile).
A net named `logic` is legal IEEE 1364-2005; `logic` is a reserved word under the SV profiles (spec-correct rejects there). Regression lock for the `.4.1` over-rejection closed in `.4.2`.

SV-0034: the associative-array dimension is IEEE 1800 §7.8 only — IEEE 1364-2005 has no associative arrays (Annex A array dimensions are ranged only); gated at VERILOG-2005-PROFILE.6.10 (whole-rule @profiles gate on `associative_dimension`). Uses the wildcard `[*]` form (`reg q [*];`) because it UNIQUELY isolates `associative_dimension`: the `[data_type]` form with a type keyword (e.g. `[integer]`) routes through `unpacked_dimension`'s expression instead — a separate keyword-as-primary leak tracked as SV-0035 — while `[*]` matches only the associative wildcard alternative.

SV-0022 lock: `module m; bind target_mod my_checker c1(); endmodule` — a spec-valid single-`;` `bind` inside a module. FIXED at SV-OVER-REJECTION-FIDELITY.2 (1.0.166): the redundant trailing `semi` in `bind_directive` (grammars/systemverilog.ebnf:668/:670) was removed — every `bind_instantiation` alternative (module/program/interface/checker_instantiation) already consumes its own `;`, so the LRM's `bind … bind_instantiation ;` is a redundant double-`;` that all commercial tools resolve as a single `;`. Now ACCEPTS under sv_2017/sv_2023 (`bind` is IEEE 1800 only) and REJECTS under verilog_2005 (no `bind` in IEEE 1364-2005 Annex A — the SV-only-construct-rejects-under-v2005 pattern). Before the fix it wrongly REJECTED under every profile (over-rejection); it stays in reject/ because the file name tracks the verilog_2005 verdict.

SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.4 (ledger SV-0069): the BLOCK-scope half, reached through `block_data_type` rather than `data_type` — a SECOND grammar site carrying the same `integer_atom_type ( signing )?` shape, so a fix applied to one site only leaves this live. IEEE 1364-2005 A.2.8 `block_item_declaration` (…Annex_A…txt:314) is `{ attribute_instance } integer list_of_block_variable_identifiers ;`; only :313's `reg [ signed ] [ range ]` takes signing inside a block.
The first SV-only family gated (`.2`); also the alias-normalization reject probe.

`#1step` delay_value is IEEE 1800-only (A.2.2.3); IEEE 1364-2005 delay_value is unsigned_number | real_number | identifier, and a faithful 1364-2005 lexer cannot even form `1step`. Reject-lock for the `SV-0025` fix (`.6.2`): before the fix this wrongly ACCEPTED under `verilog_2005` via the un-gated `delay_value` branch.
`#10ns` time-literal delay is IEEE 1800-only; 1364-2005 has no time literals. Second `SV-0025` reject-lock (the `time_literal` sibling branch of the same `delay_value_sv_only` lift).

IEEE 1800 A.8.4 bare-`$` primary (`x = $;`) — SystemVerilog-only (1364-2005 A.8.4 has no `$` primary; semantic queue-bound restriction stays out of parser scope). SV-0029 wave-3 lock: accepts under the SV profiles via the profile-gated `primary_dollar_sv_only` lift; rejects under verilog_2005.

IEEE 1800 §20.11 module-level elaboration severity task `$fatal;` — SystemVerilog-only. SV-0029 wave-3 lock: accepts under sv_2017 (elaboration_system_task_sv_2017) / sv_2023 (severity_system_task_sv_2023) now that the four severity token literals carry their `$` spellings; rejects under verilog_2005 because both host rules are profile-tagged out (no gate change needed — the .4 probe matrix disproved the earlier `.1` leak hypothesis: the mangled `sv_dollar_fatal;` had been accepting as an ordinary implicit-type variable declaration, not through the severity host).

IEEE 1800 §3.12 `$root.`-anchored hierarchical name — SystemVerilog-only. SV-0029 wave-3 lock: under the SV profiles `$root.m.y` now routes through the profile-gated `hierarchical_root_prefix_sv_only` prefix of `hierarchical_identifier` (the AST carries the explicit root marker instead of the pre-fix generic system_tf steal); under verilog_2005 the prefix is gated off AND the system_tf_call steal-guard withdraws the generic reading of `$root.`, so the file rejects — pre-fix it wrongly ACCEPTED under verilog_2005 via the steal.

IEEE 1800 §3.12.1 `$unit::` compilation-unit scope — SystemVerilog-only (1364-2005 has no $unit). SV-0029 wave-3 lock (SV-DOLLAR-LRM-FIDELITY.4): the LRM spelling now ACCEPTS under the SV profiles via the profile-gated `package_scope_dollar_unit_sv_only` lift and REJECTS under verilog_2005; pre-fix it was wrongly rejected everywhere (the token literal was the mangled `sv_dollar_unit`).

SV-0033: the bare `[]` (unsized) dimension of a dynamic array (`reg q [];`) is IEEE 1800 §7.5 only — IEEE 1364-2005 array dimensions are always ranged (`[msb:lsb]`), with no unsized dimension anywhere in Annex A; gated at VERILOG-2005-PROFILE.6.9 (whole-rule @profiles gate on `unsized_dimension`).

`-> #5 e;` is legal in NO dialect: per IEEE 1800 A.6.5 the optional `[ delay_or_event_control ]` belongs to the NONBLOCKING `->>` form ONLY, and IEEE 1364-2005 has no delay-form trigger at all. RE-ADJUDICATED at SV-OVER-REJECTION-FIDELITY.3 (SV-0023): the prior sv_2017/sv_2023 `accept` rows recorded the over-acceptance defect (the delay control was mis-attached to a second `->` branch); the fix moved the control onto `->>`, so `-> #5 e;` now correctly REJECTS under every profile.

SV-0023 lock: `->> e;` nonblocking event trigger (IEEE 1800 §15.5.4 / A.6.5). ACCEPTS under sv_2017/sv_2023 (closed at SV-OVER-REJECTION-FIDELITY.3 by adding the `->>` (nonblocking_implies) token — the literal `->>` was previously absent from the grammar). REJECTS under verilog_2005 (IEEE 1364-2005 has no `->>`; the SV-only-construct-rejects-under-v2005 pattern). File name tracks the verilog_2005 verdict.

SV-0023 lock: `->> #5 e;` nonblocking event trigger with `[ delay_or_event_control ]` (IEEE 1800 A.6.5 — the control belongs to `->>` ONLY). ACCEPTS under sv_2017/sv_2023 (the optional control is now on the nonblocking branch). REJECTS under verilog_2005 (no `->>` / no delay-form trigger in IEEE 1364-2005). File name tracks the verilog_2005 verdict.

A time literal as an expression primary (`assign w = 10ns;`) is IEEE 1800-only. Reject-lock for the `SV-0027` fix (`.6.2`): `primary_literal`'s SV-only `time_literal` branch was un-gated under `verilog_2005`.

An unbased-unsized literal (`'0`, IEEE 1800 §5.7.1) does not exist in IEEE 1364-2005. Second `SV-0027` reject-lock (the `unbased_unsized_literal` sibling branch of the same `primary_literal_sv_only` lift).
Statement-body `foreach` form (non-reinterpretable as any 1364-2005 construct).
SV-0032: void function return type is IEEE 1800 only (1364-2005 has no void return type); gated at VERILOG-2005-PROFILE.6.8.

Uses the non-reinterpretable `assert (1) else $error(...)` action-block form: a bare `initial assert (1);` is a legal 1364-2005 task enable (see the accept corpus), per feedback_corpus_expected_from_spec_not_fix.

SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.4 (ledger SV-0069): IEEE 1364-2005 A.2.1.3 `integer_declaration ::= integer list_of_variable_identifiers ;` (…Annex_A…txt:152) admits no signing, and neither `signing` nor `integer_atom_type` appears anywhere in that Annex — signing on an integer ATOM is IEEE 1800 A.2.2.1 only. Gated by a profile-gated alias on the OPTIONAL (`integer_atom_signing_sv_only`), never on `integer_atom_type` itself, which must stay reachable so plain `integer i;` still parses. Two-sided by construction: the same text must still ACCEPT under both SV profiles.

ANSI form `input interconnect w` — rejects under verilog_2005 (no `interconnect` net type). SV-0024 (the un-braced non-ANSI `module m (a b);` form) is now FIXED at SV-LRM-SHAPE-FIDELITY.1; the bare form is locked separately by `reject/port_bare_multi_id.sv`.
Uses `return x;` (argument form): a bare `return;` is a legal 1364-2005 task enable of a task named `return`, per feedback_corpus_expected_from_spec_not_fix.
SV-0031: a package→class nested scope-resolution call (`p::C::f();`) — two `::` operators, IEEE 1800 only; gated at VERILOG-2005-PROFILE.6.11 (whole-rule @profiles gate on `scope_resolution`).

SV-0031: the `::` scope-resolution operator (here a package-scoped subroutine call `p::f();`) is IEEE 1800 (SystemVerilog) only — IEEE 1364-2005 has no `::` token anywhere in Annex A; gated at VERILOG-2005-PROFILE.6.11 (whole-rule @profiles gate on `scope_resolution`, the single `::` producer).

SV-0031: a package-scoped constant expression (`wire w = p::X;`) — the `::` scope-resolution surface in expression context, IEEE 1800 only; gated at VERILOG-2005-PROFILE.6.11 (whole-rule @profiles gate on `scope_resolution`).

SV-0024 lock: `module m (a b);` — an un-braced multi-identifier port_expression. IEEE `port_expression ::= port_reference | { port_reference {, port_reference} }` requires literal concatenation braces, so `a b` is invalid under verilog_2005 (only the non-ANSI port_expression path exists there). Under sv_2017/sv_2023 it ACCEPTS as a legitimate ANSI interface port (`a` = interface_identifier, `b` = port_identifier; the not-a-declared-interface check is elaboration, not parse). Fixed at SV-LRM-SHAPE-FIDELITY.1.
SV-0034: the queue dimension `[$]` (`reg q [$];`) is IEEE 1800 §7.10 only — IEEE 1364-2005 has no queues; gated at VERILOG-2005-PROFILE.6.10 (whole-rule @profiles gate on `queue_dimension`).
The mangled non-language spelling `sv_dollar_setup(...)` must REJECT everywhere — the SV-0029 wave-1 reject-lock pinning that the pre-fix over-acceptance stays closed.

SV-0028 lock: a bare top-level `;`. IEEE 1364-2005 A.1.2 `source_text ::= { description }` with `description ::= module_declaration | udp_declaration | config_declaration` admits no null/empty top-level item, so a stray `;` is invalid under verilog_2005 — it accepted only via `source_text_item`'s LRM-less direct `semi` branch, removed at SV-LRM-SHAPE-FIDELITY.2. Under sv_2017/sv_2023 it correctly ACCEPTS as the LRM empty package-or-generate item (`description ::= … | { attribute_instance } package_item`, `package_or_generate_item_declaration ::= … | ;` — IEEE 1800-2017 §26 / 2023 Annex A), reached via the PEG-first `description` path that is untouched by the fix. SV-profile-byte-invariant (no release bump).

SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.4 (ledger SV-0069): the SECOND atom `integer_atom_type` reaches under verilog_2005. IEEE 1364-2005 A.2.1.3 `time_declaration ::= time list_of_variable_identifiers ;` (…Annex_A…txt:174) admits no signing either, so a gate written only for the `integer` spelling would leave this one accepting.
`e == 1'b` (digit-less rhs) is neither a scalar_constant nor an expression — REJECT everywhere, before and after the SV-0030 fix.
The digit-less non-language text `initial q = 1'b;` must REJECT everywhere — the SV-0030 reject-lock pinning that the pre-fix over-acceptance stays closed.
SV-0032: the void'(...) cast is IEEE 1800 only; gated at VERILOG-2005-PROFILE.6.8.
Uses the `else`-action form task enables cannot take; a plain `wait_order (a, b);` is a legal 1364-2005 task enable (see the accept corpus).
